summary: Iteration 18 — full backend + frontend testing of (1) public gig sharing, (2) per-gig role + crew, (3) admin user management & read-only admin security. 24/24 backend pytest tests pass; all critical UI flows verified end-to-end.

minor.issue: The 'cancelled gig returns 404' branch (server.py L2828-2830) is currently unreachable from the API surface — GigPatch does not include `status`, and DELETE /api/gigs/{id} removes the gig entirely. The check is correct but defensively dead code. If admin-cancel is intended, expose a PATCH/POST endpoint that sets status='cancelled'.
Toast on the admin UI just shows 'Role: lead' — could be clearer (e.g. 'Role updated to Lead for Iter18 A'). Minor UX.

issues: Renders cleanly with HCOB Network branding, $25/hr pill, location, when, slots, description. Claim CTA + 'Sign up free →' link both visible and correctly point to /app/gigs/{id} and /register?next=/app/gigs/{id} respectively. Address is correctly stripped.

action_items: (Optional) Expose a way to set gig.status='cancelled' (PATCH endpoint or dedicated /cancel) — the public_gig_lookup already handles this status but no caller can produce it.
(Optional) Improve the role-change toast wording in admin GigDetail (currently just 'Role: lead').
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 4195 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into routers (gigs/, admin/, public/, workers/, settings/) — would also reduce merge risk between iter18 features.
Public lookup correctly excludes `address_line` and other PII (confirmed by test_address_stripped).
require_admin RO-blocking applies to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE — confirmed for /api/gigs (POST blocked) and /api/admin/admins/{id} (PUT & DELETE blocked).
GET /api/gigs/{gig_id} crew logic attaches `crew` only when my_acceptance.status==APPROVED — verified excludes self and only exposes first_name + gig_role. No last-name leak.

Self-protection on admin endpoints (cannot demote/read-only/delete self) tested green; verify last-full-admin protection is also covered — currently only enforced via count in delete; the test_iter18 test_delete_admin works because there are >2 full admins, but a single-admin teardown could fail. Consider a dedicated unit test for the 'last full admin' branch using a transactional DB fixture.
